requirements.trigger: Sales sends an inbound buyer security questionnaire to the compliance manager
requirements.happyPath: Sales forwards the questionnaire; the compliance manager assembles answers, chasing engineers for specifics; legal reviews the buyer's DPA; redlines are exchanged over two rounds; the contract is signed and the account provisioned.

requirements.title: Legal reviews the buyer's data processing addendum before signature
requirements.description: Step 3 of the mid-market business process requires legal review of the buyer-supplied data processing addendum.
requirements.quote: 3. Legal reviews the buyer's data processing addendum

requirements.title: Two rounds of redlines are typical before signature
requirements.description: Contract negotiation for mid-market deals typically involves two rounds of exchanged redlines before the contract is signed.
requirements.quote: 4. Redlines exchanged, typically two rounds

requirements.title: Account provisioned on contract signature
requirements.description: Once the contract is signed, the customer account is provisioned.
requirements.quote: 5. Contract signed, account provisioned

requirements.title: No compliance interaction between signature and renewal
requirements.description: After provisioning, there is no further compliance interaction with a mid-market customer until the renewal event.
requirements.quote: 6. No further compliance interaction until renewal

requirements.title: Mid-market compliance complexity rated moderate
requirements.description: The mid-market persona is classified as moderate compliance complexity, driving the level of process and review applied.
requirements.quote: **Compliance Complexity:** Moderate

requirements.title: SOC 2 Type II report required before contract signature
requirements.description: Enterprise buyers require a SOC 2 Type II report to be provided before signature, with no exceptions permitted. The report must also be available at the point where the security review begins, ahead of technical evaluation.
requirements.quote: Requires SOC 2 Type II report before signature, no exceptions

requirements.title: SOC 2 Type II requested before technical evaluation
requirements.description: For enterprise buyers, the SOC 2 Type II report is requested before the technical evaluation stage begins, making it a gating artifact early in the sales cycle.
requirements.quote: SOC 2 Type II report requested before technical evaluation begins

requirements.title: Absence of Type II report halts the procurement process
requirements.description: If no SOC 2 Type II report exists, the enterprise procurement process stops. A SOC 2 Type I report is accepted only rarely and only subject to conditions.
requirements.quote: Absence of a Type II report halts the process; a Type I is accepted only rarely and with conditions

requirements.title: Subprocessor list disclosure with right to object
requirements.description: Enterprise customers review the subprocessor list during vendor assessment and retain a contractual right to object to newly added subprocessors.
requirements.quote: Subprocessor list reviewed, with a right to object to additions

requirements.title: 30-day advance notice of subprocessor changes
requirements.description: Any change to the subprocessor list must be notified to enterprise customers 30 days in advance of the change taking effect.
requirements.quote: notification of any subprocessor change 30 days ahead

requirements.title: Annual penetration test summary required
requirements.description: Enterprise buyers require an annual penetration test summary as part of the security review evidence package.
requirements.quote: Annual penetration test summary required

requirements.title: Right to audit clause in enterprise contracts
requirements.description: Most enterprise contracts include a negotiated right-to-audit clause granting the customer audit rights over the vendor.
requirements.quote: Right to audit clause negotiated in most contracts

requirements.title: Contractual incident notification window of 24 to 72 hours
requirements.description: Enterprise contracts commonly impose an incident notification window of 24 to 72 hours, which is shorter than the applicable regulatory minimum.
requirements.quote: Incident notification window commonly 24 to 72 hours, shorter than the regulatory minimum

requirements.title: Enterprise compliance timeline of 6 to 11 weeks
requirements.description: The expected compliance and procurement timeline for enterprise buyers is 6 to 11 weeks, and this segment is where deals most commonly stall.
requirements.quote: Expected timeline: 6-11 weeks, and this is where deals stall

requirements.title: Annual reassessment with ongoing notification obligations
requirements.description: Enterprise customers perform an annual reassessment of the vendor, supplemented by continuous notification obligations throughout the contract term.
requirements.quote: Monitoring: annual reassessment, plus notification obligations throughout

requirements.title: Data processing addendum and security exhibit negotiation
requirements.description: Enterprise deals require negotiation of a data processing addendum and a security exhibit before contract signature.
requirements.quote: Data processing addendum and security exhibit negotiated

requirements.title: Architecture review with customer security team
requirements.description: The enterprise procurement process includes an architecture review conducted jointly with the customer's security team.
requirements.quote: Architecture review with the customer's security team

requirements.title: Enterprise buyer vendor risk assessment journey
requirements.description: End-to-end enterprise purchase journey: a business sponsor identifies the need, procurement opens a vendor risk assessment, security review requests evidence, architecture review occurs, DPA and security exhibit are negotiated, the contract is signed with notification and audit obligations, and annual reassessment follows.
requirements.quote: Business sponsor identifies the need; procurement opens a vendor risk assessment
requirements.actor: Enterprise buyer (business sponsor, procurement, CISO, legal)
requirements.trigger: Business sponsor identifies a need and procurement opens a vendor risk assessment
requirements.happyPath: Procurement opens the assessment, security review receives SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary and subprocessor list, architecture review is completed with the customer security team, the DPA and security exhibit are negotiated, the contract is signed with notification and audit obligations, and annual reassessment plus 30-day subprocessor change notices follow.

requirements.title: Security review evidence package
requirements.description: The enterprise security review requests a defined evidence set: SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summary, and subprocessor list.
requirements.quote: Security review requests SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary, subprocessor list

requirements.title: Enterprise segment profile and data scope
requirements.description: Enterprise buyers span 500-4,000 seats with formal vendor risk management, and handle employee personal information at scale plus content subject to their own regulatory obligations.
requirements.quote: Data: employee personal information at scale, and content subject to their own regulatory obligations

requirements.title: Customer regulator expectations flow down into Northwind contracts
requirements.description: Regulated enterprise buyers in financial services or healthcare pass their own regulator's expectations through into the contract with Northwind, so contractual obligations must accommodate third-party regulatory requirements.
requirements.quote: Their own regulator's expectations flow down into Northwind's contract

requirements.title: SOC 2 Type II report plus supplementary control evidence
requirements.description: Regulated enterprise buyers require a SOC 2 Type II report and, in addition, evidence of specific controls that goes beyond what the report contains.
requirements.quote: SOC 2 Type II plus evidence of specific controls beyond the report

requirements.title: Data residency commitments for EU or in-country storage
requirements.description: The platform must make contractual data residency commitments, including EU-specific or in-country data location requirements for regulated enterprise buyers.
requirements.quote: Data residency commitments, with EU or in-country requirements

requirements.title: Customer-managed encryption keys not currently supported
requirements.description: Regulated enterprise buyers request customer-managed encryption keys, but the platform does not currently support this capability — an identified gap.
requirements.quote: Customer-managed encryption keys requested; not currently supported

requirements.title: 24-hour incident notification window
requirements.description: Regulated enterprise buyers require incident notification windows as short as 24 hours, which the contract and incident response process must be able to meet.
requirements.quote: Incident notification as short as 24 hours

requirements.title: Right to audit exercised in practice
requirements.description: Regulated enterprise buyers do not merely hold contractual audit rights — they actually exercise them, so the organisation must be prepared for real audits, not just clauses.
requirements.quote: Right to audit exercised in practice, not just contractually

requirements.title: Expected sales/compliance timeline of 3-6 months
requirements.description: The end-to-end engagement timeline for a regulated enterprise buyer is expected to be 3 to 6 months.
requirements.quote: Expected timeline: 3-6 months

requirements.title: Continuous monitoring with quarterly reviews and annual audit
requirements.description: Regulated enterprise buyers require continuous monitoring, supplemented by quarterly reviews and an annual audit conducted either on-site or remotely.
requirements.quote: Monitoring: continuous, with quarterly reviews and annual on-site or remote audit

requirements.title: Relationship-led acquisition journey for regulated enterprise buyer
requirements.description: The regulated enterprise buyer is acquired via referral or outbound rather than self-serve, progressing through a preliminary compliance conversation, gap assessment, remediation commitments, executive sponsorship, contracting, and ongoing oversight.
requirements.quote: Referral or outbound; relationship-led rather than self-serve
requirements.actor: Regulated Enterprise Buyer (CISO, compliance, external auditor)
requirements.trigger: Referral or outbound contact from a financial services or healthcare organisation
requirements.happyPath: Referral or outbound contact leads to a preliminary compliance conversation, a gap assessment against the customer's control expectations, remediation commitments, executive sponsorship on both sides, and a contract with audit rights, notification windows and residency commitments, followed by quarterly reviews and an annual audit.

requirements.title: Preliminary compliance conversation precedes technical work
requirements.description: For regulated enterprise buyers, a preliminary compliance conversation must take place before any technical work begins.
requirements.quote: Preliminary compliance conversation before any technical work

requirements.title: Gap assessment against customer control expectations
requirements.description: A gap assessment must be performed comparing Northwind's controls against the regulated enterprise customer's stated control expectations.
requirements.quote: Gap assessment against the customer's control expectations

requirements.title: Remediation commitments with contractual deadlines
requirements.description: Gaps identified must be closed through remediation commitments, which are sometimes bound to deadlines written into the contract.
requirements.quote: Remediation commitments, sometimes with contractual deadlines

requirements.title: Executive sponsorship required on both sides
requirements.description: Engagements with regulated enterprise buyers require executive sponsorship from both Northwind and the customer.
requirements.quote: Executive sponsorship on both sides

requirements.title: Contract must include audit rights, notification windows and residency commitments
requirements.description: The executed contract with a regulated enterprise buyer must contain audit rights, incident notification windows, and data residency commitments.
requirements.quote: Contract with audit rights, notification windows and residency commitments

requirements.title: Immediate notification of material change
requirements.description: Ongoing obligations for regulated enterprise buyers include quarterly review, annual audit, and immediate notification of any material change.
requirements.quote: Ongoing: quarterly review, annual audit, immediate notification of material change

requirements.title: Continuous automated evidence collection tied to controls
requirements.description: Evidence for controls must be collected continuously and automatically, with each item linked to the specific control it evidences, rather than gathered retrospectively at audit time.
requirements.quote: Evidence collected continuously and automatically, tied to the control it evidences

requirements.title: Missing evidence periods surfaced within days of period close
requirements.description: Any period for which control evidence is missing must be identified and surfaced within days of that period closing, not discovered during the audit.
requirements.quote: Missing periods surfaced within days of the period closing, not at audit

requirements.title: Evidence immutable once collected
requirements.description: Once an evidence item has been collected it must be immutable and cannot be altered.
requirements.quote: Evidence immutable once collected

requirements.title: Controls must be evidenced as operating throughout the report period
requirements.description: Because a Type II report covers a period of time, controls must be demonstrated to have operated continuously throughout that entire period rather than only at a point in time.
requirements.quote: A Type II report covers a period. Controls must be shown to have operated throughout it, and Northwind has been collecting evidence at the end.

requirements.title: Missed access review in a quarter becomes a report exception
requirements.description: A quarter in which an access review was not performed cannot be remediated retrospectively; it is recorded as an exception in the audit report.
requirements.quote: A quarter with a missed access review cannot be fixed retrospectively; it becomes an exception in the report

requirements.title: Impersonation must be tied to a customer-linked ticket
requirements.description: Support engineer impersonation sessions may only be initiated when tied to a ticket linked to the customer account being accessed, replacing the current ability to enter any account freely.
requirements.quote: Impersonation tied to a customer-linked ticket

requirements.title: Impersonation sessions are read-only by default
requirements.description: By default an impersonation session grants read-only access to the customer account; write capability is not available without further authorisation.
requirements.quote: Read-only by default; write requires a second approver

requirements.title: Write access during impersonation requires a second approver
requirements.description: Elevating an impersonation session to allow write actions requires approval from a second approver.
requirements.quote: Read-only by default; write requires a second approver

requirements.title: Customer-visible log for every impersonation session
requirements.description: The system must produce a log of every impersonation session that is visible to the customer whose account was accessed. An enterprise deal specifically requested this capability.
requirements.quote: Customer-visible log for every session

requirements.title: Actions attributed to the impersonating engineer
requirements.description: Any action taken during an impersonation session must be attributed in logs and records to the support engineer performing it, not to the customer user being impersonated.
requirements.quote: Actions attributed to the engineer, not the customer

requirements.title: Support engineer accesses a customer account under impersonation controls
requirements.description: A support engineer needing to investigate a customer issue opens a customer-linked ticket, enters the account in read-only impersonation, requests a second approver if write access is needed, and the session is logged visibly to the customer with actions attributed to the engineer.
requirements.quote: Support engineers can currently enter any account. It is efficient, and it is the single control most likely to fail an enterprise review.
requirements.trigger: Support engineer needs to access a customer account to resolve an issue
requirements.happyPath: Engineer opens a customer-linked ticket, starts a read-only impersonation session, obtains a second approver for any write action, and the session appears in the customer-visible log with all actions attributed to the engineer.

requirements.title: Impersonation controls must not block self-serve support volume
requirements.description: Because self-serve customers generate most impersonation volume, the control design must avoid a blanket restriction that would degrade support operations.
requirements.quote: Self-serve customers generate most impersonation volume, so a blanket restriction would hurt support

requirements.title: Ability to answer who can see customer data and under what circumstances
requirements.description: The organisation must be able to honestly answer enterprise reviewer questions about who can access customer data and the circumstances under which access occurs — a capability that does not exist today.
requirements.quote: Cannot answer "who can see our data and under what circumstances" honestly today

requirements.title: Central answer library linked to controls
requirements.description: Security questionnaire answers must be maintained in a central repository, each answer associated with the control it describes, rather than being answered ad hoc from memory per deal.
requirements.quote: Answers maintained centrally against the control they describe

requirements.title: Answers refreshed on control change, not on questionnaire arrival
requirements.description: An answer must be updated at the time the underlying control changes, rather than being revised reactively when a new questionnaire is received. This prevents answers drifting from the actual state of the platform.
requirements.quote: Answer updated when the control changes, not when a questionnaire arrives

requirements.title: Evidence linked to each questionnaire answer
requirements.description: Each answer in the library must have supporting evidence linked to it so that any claim made to a customer can be substantiated.
requirements.quote: Evidence linked to each answer so a claim can be substantiated

requirements.title: Consistent answers across deals
requirements.description: The same question answered for different deals must produce consistent answers; inconsistency between deals is itself an audit finding when a customer notices.
requirements.quote: Inconsistent answers between deals, which is itself a finding when a customer notices

requirements.title: Reduce questionnaire effort below current 8-15 hour baseline
requirements.description: Current process consumes 8-15 hours of effort per mid-market deal responding to security questionnaires; the centralized answer approach targets reducing this burden.
requirements.quote: 8-15 hours per mid-market deal

requirements.title: Support multi-tenant scale of 2,400 customer organisations
requirements.description: The platform's controls and isolation mechanisms must operate across a base of 2,400 customer organisations, which sets the baseline scale for tenant separation and reporting.
requirements.quote: Customer organisations: 2,400

requirements.title: Production access population limited to 31 internal users
requirements.description: Only 31 internal users hold production access, defining the population over which access control, review and revocation processes must operate.
requirements.quote: Internal users with production access: 31

requirements.title: Access grant volume of 40-70 per month
requirements.description: The access provisioning process must handle between 40 and 70 access grants per month, each of which needs to be authorised and evidenced.
requirements.quote: Access grants per month: 40-70

requirements.title: Support impersonation session volume of 900-1,400 per month
requirements.description: Between 900 and 1,400 support impersonation sessions occur each month, so any logging, consent or monitoring control over impersonation must scale to that volume.
requirements.quote: Support impersonation sessions per month: 900-1,400

requirements.title: CCPA request volume of 3-12 per month and rising
requirements.description: The privacy request handling process must cope with 3 to 12 CCPA requests per month, with volume expected to increase.
requirements.quote: CCPA requests per month: 3-12, rising

requirements.title: Security questionnaire volume of 6-14 per month
requirements.description: The organisation receives between 6 and 14 security questionnaires per month, which must be answered from documented control evidence.
requirements.quote: Security questionnaires per month: 6-14

requirements.title: Deployment volume of 30-60 per week
requirements.description: Change management controls must accommodate 30 to 60 production deployments per week.
requirements.quote: Deployments per week: 30-60

requirements.title: Incident volume of 2-6 per month with at most one customer-affecting
requirements.description: Between 2 and 6 incidents occur per month, of which 0 to 1 affect customers, setting the baseline for incident response and customer notification workload.
requirements.quote: Incidents per month: 2-6, of which 0-1 are customer-affecting

requirements.title: Controls must be operable by a team of three
requirements.description: The compliance and security programme is staffed by two security engineers and one compliance manager, so all controls must be sustainable within that staffing level.
requirements.quote: two security engineers and one compliance manager

requirements.title: Avoid controls requiring sustained manual effort
requirements.description: Any control that depends on sustained manual effort will lapse given the available staffing, and a lapsed control is worse than an absent one because it surfaces in the audit report as an exception. Controls must therefore be automated or otherwise self-sustaining.
requirements.quote: Anything requiring sustained manual effort will lapse, and a lapsed control is worse than an absent one because it appears in the report as an exception.

requirements.title: Enterprise security review cleared in under 3 weeks
requirements.description: Enterprise security reviews must complete in less than 3 weeks, reduced from the current baseline of 6-11 weeks.
requirements.quote: Enterprise security review cleared in under 3 weeks, from 6-11

requirements.title: Questionnaire response time under 2 hours per deal
requirements.description: Security questionnaire responses must be produced in under 2 hours per deal, down from the current 8-15 hours.
requirements.quote: Questionnaire response time under 2 hours per deal, from 8-15

requirements.title: No deals lost for lack of a Type II report
requirements.description: Zero deals may be lost due to the absence of a SOC 2 Type II report.
requirements.quote: Zero deals lost for absence of a Type II report

requirements.title: Subprocessor notifications issued 30 days in advance
requirements.description: Every subprocessor change notification must be issued 30 days ahead of the change, with no exceptions.
requirements.quote: Subprocessor notifications issued 30 days ahead, every time

requirements.title: Complete evidence coverage across the audit window
requirements.description: Evidence must exist for every control for every period covered by the audit window.
requirements.quote: Evidence present for every control for every period in the audit window

requirements.title: Zero exceptions in the first Type II report
requirements.description: The first SOC 2 Type II report must be issued with zero exceptions.
requirements.quote: Zero exceptions in the first Type II report

requirements.title: Deprovisioning within 24 hours
requirements.description: Access deprovisioning must occur within 24 hours and be measurable with no unexplained gaps in the record.
requirements.quote: Deprovisioning within 24 hours, measured with no unexplained gaps

requirements.title: CCPA request acknowledgement within 10 business days
requirements.description: Consumer privacy requests under CCPA must be acknowledged within 10 business days of receipt.
requirements.quote: CCPA requests acknowledged within 10 business days and answered within 45

requirements.title: CCPA request substantive response within 45 days
requirements.description: Consumer privacy requests under CCPA must be answered within 45 days.
requirements.quote: CCPA requests acknowledged within 10 business days and answered within 45

requirements.title: Monthly uptime of 99.9%
requirements.description: The service must achieve 99.9% uptime measured monthly.
requirements.quote: Uptime 99.9% monthly

requirements.title: Quarterly verified restore test
requirements.description: Backup restore must be tested quarterly, with a verified real restore rather than a paper exercise.
requirements.quote: Restore tested quarterly with a verified real restore

requirements.title: All impersonation sessions ticket-linked
requirements.description: 100% of impersonation sessions must be linked to a ticket.
requirements.quote: Impersonation sessions 100% ticket-linked

requirements.title: Define start of SOC 2 Type II observation period
requirements.description: The business must decide and document when the Type II observation period begins — at implementation of controls, or once evidence collection can be demonstrated to be continuous. Open question requiring resolution before audit planning.
requirements.quote: When does the Type II observation period start — at implementation, or when evidence collection is demonstrably continuous?

requirements.title: Scope of Global Privacy Control honouring
requirements.description: A decision is required on whether Global Privacy Control signals are honoured universally for all users, or only for users in jurisdictions where CCPA applies.
requirements.quote: Do we honour Global Privacy Control for every user, or only where CCPA applies?

requirements.title: Customer-visible impersonation log timing
requirements.description: A decision is required on whether the customer-visible impersonation log is exposed in real time or intentionally delayed so as not to reveal an active investigation.
requirements.quote: Is a customer-visible impersonation log real time, or delayed to avoid revealing an active investigation?

requirements.title: Customer-managed encryption keys commitment and timeline
requirements.description: A decision is required on whether to commit to customer-managed encryption keys for regulated buyers, and on what delivery timeline if committed.
requirements.quote: Do we commit to customer-managed encryption keys for regulated buyers, and if so on what timeline?

requirements.title: Classification of subprocessor changes requiring 30-day notice
requirements.description: The business must define which subprocessor changes trigger the 30-day advance notice obligation, and which changes are routine enough to be notified after the fact.
requirements.quote: Which subprocessor changes require the 30-day notice, and which are routine enough to notify after the fact?
